newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Eight feared dead after barge sinks on Danube.
newsitem.headline: Eight feared dead after barge sinks on Danube.

text.p: Eight men were missing and feared dead after their barge crashed into a weir at a hydroelectric powerstation in high water on the Danube in Vienna late on Tuesday, Austrian police said on Wednesday.
Firemen and divers called to the scene found only one severly injured survivor. The search for the eight missing sailors was called off after several hours, they said.
A police spokeswoman told Reuters the search would resume early on Wednesday and would be extended to the Slovak border, about 50 km (30 miles) downriver.

The barge, registered in the Slovak Republic, capsized and sank immediately after running into the weir, she said. There was no damage to the powerstation, which supplies most of Vienna's electricity needs.

The Danube was carrying high water after heavy rainfalls over the past few days, but was still open for commercial traffic. The river is one of the most heavily-used shipping routes linking western and eastern Europe.
